clue.text: Finest on tumbling class trains, and leaves with defined shape?

parts.note: the top ones are the finest

indicators.note: in a down clue something tumbling falls head over heels, so the word for class is turned upside down

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the digit read as the letter I
RY is the abbreviation for railway, which runs the trains

explanation.surface: A top student in a gymnastics class is coaching others, and leaving in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places the finest above what follows in this down clue; the turned-over class goes in the middle and the railway at the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Topiary is the art of clipping hedges and shrubs, so their foliage is cut into deliberate shapes.

clue.text: Three legs characterise this series of races here

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the place whose emblem is a triskelion of three armoured legs
second meaning: the home of the TT motorcycle races

explanation.surface: Three-legged events are what distinguish this sequence of races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legs' and 'races' suggest a relay; the three legs are a flag emblem, and the races are the Tourist Trophy motorbike event held on this Irish Sea island.
explanation.definitionFit: The island's flag shows three running legs, and it hosts the annual Tourist Trophy road races for motorcycles.

clue.text: Muscles tense during Bond flick, at core

indicators.note: something happening during another is held within its span, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to bond is to glue together
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: the core of a word is its very centre, so only the central letter of flick is wanted

parts.note: the middle letter of the five

explanation.surface: Muscles are taut throughout a James Bond film, right at its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond with a capital B looks like 007, but it is the verb meaning stick together.
explanation.definitionFit: Glutei is the anatomical plural of gluteus, the large muscles of the buttocks.

clue.text: Pound stores support British game

indicators.note: a place that stores goods keeps them inside it, so the pound holds what follows

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, like a cage
a rib is a supporting structure
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: The pound sterling props up a British game, as if a sport were funded by the currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Pound suggests money or weight, but here it is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribbage is a card game scored by moving pegs along a board.

clue.text: Town's payment method good, superior to parking in London area

parts.note: chip and PIN is the card payment system, run together as chip-pin
standard abbreviation

indicators.note: placed in the London area, the parking letter sits inside that borough's name

parts.note: Camden is a borough of north London
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A town's way of paying is fine and better than parking in London.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'superior to' means placed above, so the good letter sits on top of the borough with parking inside. Chipping Campden is a market town in the Cotswolds.
explanation.definitionFit: Chipping Campden is a small market town in Gloucestershire, famous for its honey-coloured stone high street.

clue.text: Dean's famed for such level of expertise in international churches

parts.note: standard abbreviation

indicators.note: the level of expertise sits in the run of abbreviations, so it is placed inside them

parts.note: CE is Church of England, taken twice for the plural
a dan is a grade of skill in judo and karate

explanation.surface: A dean, a churchman, is renowned for his skill across churches around the world.
explanation.walkthrough: Dean sounds like a cathedral cleric to match the churches, but he is Christopher Dean, the skater of Torvill and Dean, Olympic champions in 1984.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Dean won Olympic gold with Jayne Torvill skating a routine to Bolero, the most famous example of this discipline.

clue.text: Constant turning when asleep? It could describe husband

indicators.note: someone asleep is usually lying in bed, so the turned constant goes inside the word for bed

parts.note: where one lies asleep

indicators.note: something turning faces the other way, so the constant is read backwards

parts.note: pi is the mathematical constant

explanation.surface: A husband who tosses and turns constantly in his sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a restless spouse; any husband, like any human, walks on two feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A biped is any two-footed animal, and a man qualifies, so the word could be used of him.

clue.text: Clear out German tea gathering dust, finally

indicators.note: to gather something is to take it in, so the tea word surrounds a letter

parts.note: standard abbreviation
cha is an informal word for tea

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word just before it

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Clearing out a German tea caddy that has been collecting dust.
explanation.walkthrough: Gertcha is Cockney slang, a slurred 'get out of it', shouted to send someone away.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang exclamation is used to tell someone to go away, exactly like the imperative to clear out.

clue.text: Dainty mushrooms son repositioned

indicators.note: something repositioned is moved to a new place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the morel is an edible mushroom, made plural by the letter for son
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Delicate mushrooms, with the son moving them about the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: Dainty looks like an adjective but is the noun meaning a delicacy; only the son's letter shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: A dainty, as a noun, is a small tasty bite of food, which is what a morsel is.

clue.text: Ham still stifling outside rear of shop

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, wrapping round so as to hold something within

parts.note: inert means motionless
ex is the Latin prefix meaning out of

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its last letter

parts.note: final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A ham kept fresh by being wrapped up outside the back of a butcher's.
explanation.walkthrough: Ham reads as meat, which suits the shop; it is the adjective-like noun for a bad actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is a clumsy, overacting performer or amateur, so the word stands for unskilled.

clue.text: Riot stirring island sheep

parts.note: live in the sense of lively, energetic
standard abbreviation
a tup is a ram

explanation.surface: A riot whipped up among the sheep of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Riot here is the verb, as in running riot, partying wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: To riot can mean to revel without restraint, and to live it up is to party extravagantly.

clue.text: One having days consumed by crack, going before court?

definitions.text: One having days consumed by crack, going before court?

indicators.note: something consumed by another is swallowed up inside it

parts.note: crack means first-rate, which is A1
D for day, doubled for the plural
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone whose days are swallowed up by crack cocaine ends up in the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes a drug user; crack in the wordplay means excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A person dependent on crack cocaine is a classic case of an addict, often facing criminal charges.

clue.text: Some Scrabble recruit welcomes match against high-fliers

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the recruit surrounds the rest

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
the Royal Air Force
to fit is to match

explanation.surface: Some Scrabble tiles go to a recruit playing a match against pilots.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrabble looks like the board game, but it is a verb-turned-noun meaning scribble.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrabble is an old word for scrawling, and graffiti is scrawled writing on walls.

clue.text: Perhaps bow down in front of Don

parts.note: to neck a drink is to down it
to don clothes is to wear them

explanation.surface: Perhaps one should bow low before a university don.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow suggests a respectful gesture before an academic; it is the bow tie, and Don is the verb to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow tie is one example of an item worn around the neck.

clue.text: First testing centre, say, probing country's sports team

indicators.note: something probing pushes its way into another thing, so it goes inside

parts.note: Wales is a country of the UK
a laboratory numbered one, such as Lab 1

explanation.surface: A first testing centre probing a nation's sports team, perhaps for doping.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wallabies are Australia's rugby union side; the testing centre is Lab 1, with the numeral as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wallabies is the nickname of the Australian national rugby union team.

clue.text: Paddy's northbound where many Irish settle and retire

indicators.note: travelling north in a down clue means going up the column, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a paddy is a fit of temper, also called a pet, plus the possessive s
County Down in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: An Irishman heads north to where many of his compatriots have settled, to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy looks like an Irish name, matching the surface; it means a tantrum, and 'in a pet' is an old phrase for sulking.
explanation.definitionFit: To step down is to resign from a post, as one does on retiring.

clue.text: Bag inside ripping, as something stuck to fridge?

indicators.note: inside places the bagging word within the other one

parts.note: both are informal words for wonderful
to bag is to net, as in catching

explanation.surface: A bag tearing open, like a note stuck to the fridge door.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripping suggests tearing; it is the old-fashioned British slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Fridge notes are often held on by small magnets, so something stuck there would be clinging in this attracting way.

clue.text: Good book on love rat, Oscar, is fruity stuff

parts.note: Authorised Version of the Bible
zero in tennis scoring
a cad is a dishonourable man
O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A good book on a love rat called Oscar is pretty racy material.
explanation.walkthrough: Fruity suggests risqué, matching the love rat; here it means from a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An avocado is botanically a fruit, so its flesh is literally fruity stuff.

clue.text: Extraordinary state of sultan's seat

parts.note: over the top, excessive
a sultanate in Arabia

explanation.surface: A remarkable kingdom where a sultan sits on his throne.
explanation.walkthrough: Seat looks like a capital city; it is a padded footstool, named after the Turkish empire.
explanation.definitionFit: An ottoman is a low upholstered seat, its name taken from the empire ruled by the Turkish sultans.

clue.text: Rank men on decks ordinary alongside music producer

parts.note: ABs are able seamen
standard abbreviation
a lute is an instrument that makes music

explanation.surface: Sailors of a certain rank work on deck alongside a record producer.
explanation.walkthrough: Rank looks like a noun matching men, but it is the adjective, as in a rank amateur.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank as an adjective means complete or utter, so it is an intensifier synonymous with total.

clue.text: Jam sandwich's uppermost, as stomach empty

indicators.note: in a down clue the uppermost part of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter
qua is Latin for in the capacity of

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its contents, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: The top of a jam sandwich, eaten on an empty stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: Jam sandwich primes the spread; jam is the crush of a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam is a crowded crush of people, which is also called a squash.

clue.text: Hazel maybe recalled theatre work, harmonising

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the word runs in the reverse direction

parts.note: hazel is a type of wood
an op is an operation, done in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: An actress named Hazel remembered her stage work in which she sang in harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazel reads as a woman's name and theatre as the stage; theatre is the hospital operating room.
explanation.definitionFit: Doo-wop is a 1950s style of close vocal harmony singing using nonsense syllables.

clue.text: Record fair announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: fair means just or correct

explanation.surface: A fair's record attendance being proclaimed.
explanation.definitionFit: To record something is to put it down in writing.

clue.text: Prize bout's principal man making weight

parts.note: plum as an adjective means choice, highly prized

indicators.note: the principal letter of a word is its leading one

parts.note: first letter
a man's name

explanation.surface: The main man in a title fight is making the weight before the bout.
explanation.walkthrough: Making weight is boxing jargon, but the definition is a plain weight on a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumb bob is the lead weight hung on a cord to give a true vertical line.

clue.text: Graduate doctor dated flowery type

parts.note: Master of Arts
to doctor results is to rig them
dated means old-fashioned

explanation.surface: A graduate doctor with an old-fashioned, flowery manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor tempts as DR after a graduate; here it is the verb meaning falsify.
explanation.definitionFit: The marigold is a bright orange or yellow garden flower, so it is one kind of bloom.

clue.text: Plaything used less lawn with edges removed

indicators.note: removing the edges strips each word of its first and last letters, keeping the inside

parts.note: the inner letters
the inner letters
the inner letters

explanation.surface: A toy that sees less use on a lawn with its borders trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw is a playground plank on which children rise and fall in turn.

clue.text: Advance towards Tube in daydream

indicators.note: placed in the daydream, the tube word sits inside it

parts.note: to moon about is to daydream
a vein is a vessel or tube in the body

explanation.surface: Getting towards the London Underground while lost in a daydream.
explanation.walkthrough: Tube with a capital T looks like the London Underground; it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To move in on is to close in on or approach a target, which is advancing towards it.
